info.title: eDoctor Public API
info.description: OpenAPI 3.1 contract for the client-facing endpoints: the public doctor marketplace, the public availability slots endpoint, the public CMS page read, the public cookie/tracking consent registry, the authenticated tracking-consent record write, the password login and logout session endpoints, the patient sign-in-or-register access flow, the authenticated patient self read, and the doctor-session ERP payment path a terminal device runs (open cart, add line, checkout, hand the raw terminal answer back). Generated from the existing request validators and TypeScript response views; client repositories codegen types from this document.

servers.description: Public API root; each path carries its module segment.

get.summary: Search public marketplace doctors.

200.description: Paginated public marketplace doctor cards with applied filters.

get.summary: Search public marketplace doctors ordered by proximity.

200.description: Paginated nearby public marketplace doctor cards with applied filters.

get.summary: Get public marketplace search facets.

200.description: Facet option counts for the current public marketplace filters.

get.summary: List public marketplace doctor and professional suggestions.

200.description: Autocomplete suggestions for doctors and professionals.

get.summary: List public marketplace location suggestions.

200.description: Autocomplete location suggestions for the public marketplace.

get.summary: Get a public marketplace doctor profile.

200.description: Full public marketplace doctor profile for the selected office, with the response metrics of the last six months.

get.summary: List one page of the public reviews of a marketplace doctor.

200.description: Approved public reviews on the order of `sort` (newest first by default). `limit` is 1–50; without it, the 500 first. `q` matches every word in the patient comment, without accents or case. `mention` keeps the reviews that speak about one topic (U-91.2: six), good or bad. `total` counts every match; `nextCursor` names the next page. `reviews` is null for an unknown or non-visible doctor and [] when no approved review matches. 422 on an invalid input, 429 past the shared `doctor-reviews` budget.

get.summary: Get the totals of the public reviews of a marketplace doctor.

200.description: How many reviews there are, the five star bars from 5 down (always all five), the averages of the profile header and the topics. `summary` is null for an unknown or non-visible doctor.

get.summary: Get a single public marketplace doctor office.

200.description: A single public marketplace office with its availability, and what only this page reads: at most 12 images, the weekly hours and how to get there.

get.summary: List one page of the published articles as cards.

200.description: Cards of the published articles, newest publication first. The body, the sections and the SEO fields travel only with `GET /article/public/articles/{slug}`. `doctorId` keeps the articles of one doctor: an unknown or hidden doctor answers [] and a total of 0. `readingMinutes` is null when there is no time to show.

get.summary: List public bookable availability slots for a doctor, office and service.

200.description: Bookable slots grouped by date, in the office timezone, for `days` days starting at `date` (default 1, max 61). A date with no bookable slot is returned with an empty `slots` array. `date` is optional: without it the window opens on today of the platform calendar (Europe/Athens, by the server clock), and a `date` before that today is moved up to it — past days are never offered.

get.summary: Get the public cookie/tracking consent registry.

200.description: Every catalogued tool with its category, the platforms it applies to, and both el/en translations, plus the registry version the client stores with the decision.

post.summary: Record the signed-in user tracking-consent decision (requires session cookies).

200.description: The stored decision. Append-only: every call inserts a new audit row, so repeated calls never overwrite history. The decision is dated by the server clock at the moment it is stored (D-118): `decidedAt` in the answer is that instant. The body carries no `decidedAt`; one sent anyway is refused (422) like every unknown field.

get.summary: Get the published revision of a public content page.

200.description: The text of a non-archived page in force now (server clock), or with `edition=upcoming` the text a substantive change announced (404 when none). A legal page reports its legal version in `version` — the one a registration accepts — which a wording correction keeps; `effectiveAt` is when the text took or takes effect, and `upcoming` names the announced version and its date. When the requested language is missing the response falls back to Greek and reports the actual `language` plus `availableLanguages`.

post.summary: Sign in with email and password.

200.description: The signed-in tenant user. The active-token and refresh-token cookies are set on the response; no token is ever returned in the body. Until the password is proven, every credential refusal is the same 401 EC412: an unknown email, an account without a password credential, an email that may not sign in, a disabled credential and a wrong password cannot be told apart, so this endpoint never answers SIGN_IN_NOT_AVAILABLE. Repeated failures for one email from one IP lock that pair with 403 USER_LOCKED; a banned account is told so (403 USER_LOCKED) only after the right password; the per-IP `login` class answers 429.

post.summary: Revoke the current session (requires session cookies).

200.description: Number of refresh tokens revoked. Without `allDevices`, the session of this device ends — the refresh token of its cookie and the one that replaced it moments ago (a parallel request that rotated it, or the rotation of this very request when the access token had lapsed) — and no other device is signed out; the response clears the session cookies and never sets new ones. Send `allDevices: true` to revoke every session of the user: every other device is signed out at once, its access token included. Send `pushToken` (the native push token of this phone, as given to `registerPushDevice`) to forget this phone's push device with the session; a token of another account is ignored.

post.summary: Send an access OTP to an email or mobile phone.

200.description: Acknowledgement only. The response is identical whether or not an account exists for the identifier, so it cannot be used to probe for accounts.

post.summary: Resend the access OTP, subject to the same cooldown and send cap.

200.description: Acknowledgement only, identical in shape to the start response.

post.summary: Verify the access OTP and either sign in or request registration.

200.description: `signed-in` carries `tenantUser` and sets the session cookies; `registration-required` carries a single-use `registrationTicket` and creates nothing. A right code is spent even when the account may not sign in here, and three such accounts are refused with 401 SIGN_IN_NOT_AVAILABLE, with no cookie set and the account left unchanged: an account holding any role besides MEMBER and DOCTOR (it signs in with a password through `POST /auth/login`), an identifier the backoffice disabled (verified but no longer allowed to sign in), and a never-verified identifier of an account that may not activate itself (a doctor is activated by an admin). The role refusal comes before the ban check, so it is the same whether or not the account is banned; a banned MEMBER or DOCTOR account is 403 USER_LOCKED before its identifier is looked at.

post.summary: Verify a native Google ID token and sign in, provisioning the account when needed.

200.description: Always `signed-in`, with the session cookies set and full access granted; there is no follow-up step. A known email signs in and links the Google identity on first use; an unknown email is provisioned immediately from the token profile, so `legalAcceptance` must carry the CURRENT published versions and is validated and recorded only on that branch. Gender and date of birth stay empty because Google does not supply them. `target` selects the profile created for a new account and defaults to `patient`. Failure semantics match the OTP verify: banned is 403 USER_LOCKED, a disabled identifier or a Google subject already bound elsewhere is 401 SIGN_IN_NOT_AVAILABLE.

post.summary: Issue the nonce of one native Apple sign-in.

200.description: Pass `nonce` to the iOS sign-in as it is, and send the identity token that carries it to `POST /auth/access/apple`. It lives for 5 minutes and is spent by one successful sign-in. A deployment without Apple keys answers 401 SIGN_IN_NOT_AVAILABLE.

post.summary: Verify a native Apple identity token and sign in, provisioning the account when needed.

200.description: Always `signed-in`, with the session cookies set, the same answer as `POST /auth/access/google`. The email comes only from the signed token, never from the body. `legalAcceptance` must carry the CURRENT published versions and is judged only for a new account: its 400 spends neither the nonce nor the `authorizationCode`, so the same token may be sent again with fresh versions. Failures: 401 EC010 for a token, audience, signature or nonce that does not pass; 403 APPLE_EMAIL_UNAVAILABLE for a new account without an email; 403 APPLE_EMAIL_NOT_VERIFIED when Apple does not confirm the email; 401 SIGN_IN_NOT_AVAILABLE for another Apple ID on a linked account, a closed channel or a backoffice role; 403 USER_LOCKED when banned.

post.summary: Start the Android Apple sign-in: the address to open and the flow secret.

200.description: Open `authorizationUrl` in the in-app browser and keep `flowSecret` in memory only: it never passes through a browser or an address. The way back to the app is built by the server from `appVariant`; production and stage accept `production` alone, anything else is 422. After Apple, our page offers one link that hands the app `<scheme>://auth/apple-return?handoff=<code>`, or `?error=cancelled` / `?error=apple`. Nothing is written to the database. Answered with `Cache-Control: no-store`.

post.summary: Exchange the Android one-use code and the flow secret for a session.

200.description: Always `signed-in`, with the session cookies set, the same answer as `POST /auth/access/apple`, with the same failures and the same consent rule: a 400 leaves the code whole for one retry. The code lives for 240 seconds and is spent once; a wrong `flowSecret` burns it, so even the right one is then 401 EC010, and the person presses the Apple button again.

post.summary: Create the account behind a registration ticket and sign in.

201.description: The created tenant user, with the session cookies set. `password` is required for an email ticket and rejected for a phone ticket; `legalAcceptance` must carry the CURRENT published document versions; `target` selects the created profile and defaults to `patient`. The new account's `locale` is `language`, else the language of the request (`?lang`, then `Accept-Language`), else `el`. A `dateOfBirth` after today, or further back than 120 years, is refused with 422 before the ticket is spent (a baby born today passes).

post.summary: Send an OTP to the mobile the signed-in caller wants as its login phone (requires session cookies).

200.description: Acknowledgement of the delivery channel only; the number is never echoed back. The target account is always the session actor, so the body carries no identifier. Sending the caller own ALREADY verified number answers `alreadyVerified: true` without an SMS. An account whose phone channel the backoffice disabled (verified but no longer allowed to sign in) is refused with 401 SIGN_IN_NOT_AVAILABLE before any SMS is sent or any budget is charged, and attaching another number never re-enables that channel. A number that belongs to another account of the tenant is refused with 409 ALREADY_EXIST and the message of the register identity conflict ("Phone already exists for this tenant."), so the two flows cannot be told apart. A malformed number or an extra body property is 422; the per-IP `otp-send` class, the per-account send cap and the per-number cap shared with phone-register/phone-login answer 429.

post.summary: Resend the attach OTP to the number the challenge was started for (requires session cookies).

200.description: Acknowledgement only, identical in shape to the start response. The body is empty by contract: the number is read from the live challenge, so a resend can neither retarget it nor skip the uniqueness gate. Without a live challenge the answer is 401 TOKEN_NOT_FOUND; a phone channel the backoffice disabled answers 401 SIGN_IN_NOT_AVAILABLE before the cooldown, the send budgets and the SMS; inside the resend cooldown, over a send cap or over the per-IP `otp-send` class it is 429; the uniqueness refusal of start applies here too as 409 ALREADY_EXIST with the same message ("Phone already exists for this tenant.").

post.summary: Verify the attach OTP and promote the number to the account login phone (requires session cookies).

200.description: The updated session view of the caller, with `loginPhoneVerified` true and `loginPhoneMasked` filled; the full number never leaves auth. The code is single use and the number becomes usable for phone sign-in (D-04). A verify that REPLACES an already verified number signs every OTHER session of the account out at once, access tokens included, in the same transaction as the write; only the calling session, the one the request's refresh-token cookie names, goes on, and the response sets its fresh active-token and refresh-token cookies (never a token in the body). Without a live refresh-token cookie no session is kept and no cookie is set; a FIRST attach revokes nothing and sets no cookie. A phone channel the backoffice disabled answers 401 SIGN_IN_NOT_AVAILABLE and writes nothing. A wrong, expired or already consumed code is 401; too many wrong codes for the account or for the number is 429, as is the per-IP `otp-verify` class; a number taken by another account between start and verify is 409 ALREADY_EXIST with the same message as the register identity conflict ("Phone already exists for this tenant."); a malformed or extra body property is 422.

post.summary: Send a code to the address the signed-in caller wants as its login email (requires session cookies).

200.description: Acknowledgement of the delivery channel only; the address is never echoed back. The code goes ONLY to the new address, in the language the request names (`?lang`, then `Accept-Language`), else the account's own, else `el`; the current email stays the login email until the code is verified. The target account is always the session actor, so the body carries no identifier. Sending the caller own ALREADY verified email answers `alreadyVerified: true` without an email. Refused before any code is sent or any budget is charged, in this order: an account whose email channel the backoffice disabled (verified but no longer allowed to sign in), or whose email was never loginable while it holds a role beyond MEMBER (an admin activates that channel), with 401 SIGN_IN_NOT_AVAILABLE; an account with a linked Google or Apple sign-in with 403 EC403 and the message "Forbidden: LOGIN_EMAIL_CHANGE_PROVIDER_LINKED:<providers>", where <providers> is `GOOGLE`, `APPLE` or `GOOGLE,APPLE` (the person unlinks the provider first); an address that belongs to another account of the tenant with 409 ALREADY_EXIST and the message of the register identity conflict ("Email already exists for this tenant."); the address of a deleted account under a live abuse measure with 403 USER_LOCKED. A malformed address, one over 254 characters or an extra body property is 422; the per-IP `otp-send` class, the per-account send cap and the per-address cap shared with the email sign-in and registration answer 429.

post.summary: Resend the code to the address the email change was started for (requires session cookies).

200.description: Acknowledgement only, identical in shape to the start response. The body is empty by contract: the address is read from the live challenge, so a resend can neither retarget it nor skip a gate of start. Without a live challenge the answer is 401 TOKEN_NOT_FOUND; an email channel the backoffice disabled answers 401 SIGN_IN_NOT_AVAILABLE and a linked Google or Apple answers 403 "Forbidden: LOGIN_EMAIL_CHANGE_PROVIDER_LINKED:<providers>", both before the cooldown, the send budgets and the email; inside the resend cooldown, over a send cap or over the per-IP `otp-send` class it is 429; the uniqueness refusal of start applies here too as 409 ALREADY_EXIST with the same message ("Email already exists for this tenant.").

post.summary: Verify the code and make the address the account login email (requires session cookies).

200.description: Only `loginEmailMasked`, the new login email as its owner reads it (`e***i@example.gr`); the whole address never leaves auth. The code is single use; the address becomes the verified login email, usable for the email code and for the password of the account, which stays as it was, and the old address stops signing in. A verify that REPLACES an email the account signed in with signs every OTHER session of the account out at once, access tokens included, in the same transaction as the write; only the calling session, the one the request's refresh-token cookie names, goes on, and the response sets its fresh active-token and refresh-token cookies (never a token in the body). Without a live refresh-token cookie no session is kept and no cookie is set; a FIRST email revokes nothing and sets no cookie. A notice of the change is queued to the PREVIOUS email (to the verified login phone by SMS when there was none) and never names the new address. An email channel the backoffice disabled answers 401 SIGN_IN_NOT_AVAILABLE and a Google or Apple linked since start answers 403 "Forbidden: LOGIN_EMAIL_CHANGE_PROVIDER_LINKED:<providers>"; both write nothing. A wrong, expired or already consumed code is 401; a code burned by wrong guesses, and too many wrong codes for the account or for the address, is 403 USER_LOCKED; the per-IP `otp-verify` class is 429; an address taken by another account between start and verify is 409 ALREADY_EXIST with the same message as the register identity conflict ("Email already exists for this tenant."); a malformed or extra body property is 422.

get.summary: List the live sessions of the signed-in caller, the devices it is signed in from (requires session cookies).

200.description: The live sessions of the caller own account, one entry per signed-in device: the session the request came from first (`current: true`, the one its refresh-token cookie belongs to), then the most recently active. `sessionId` is stable for as long as the device stays signed in and is the only identifier of a session a client ever holds; `lastActiveAt` is the last time the session renewed. The device is described by three closed vocabularies only: `kind` (`APP` for the eDoctor app, `WEB` for a browser), `os` (`IOS`, `IPADOS`, `ANDROID`, `MACOS`, `WINDOWS`, `LINUX`, `OTHER`) and `browser` (`CHROME`, `SAFARI`, `FIREFOX`, `EDGE`, `OTHER`, and `null` for the app). They are read from the `x-device` request header when it carries `iphone-app`, `ipad-app` or `android-app` (any other value is ignored), else from the User-Agent; a device that names nothing is `WEB` / `OTHER` / `OTHER`. No User-Agent, IP address, token or row id is ever part of the answer, and the wording a person reads is composed by the client. The answer is sent with `Cache-Control: no-store`. At most the 50 newest sessions are listed.

post.summary: Sign one OTHER device of the signed-in caller out (requires session cookies).

200.description: The `sessionId` that was ended. Only that session ends: every other session of the account, the calling one included, goes on untouched. The ended device is refused quietly (401, cookies cleared) the next time it renews its session, and its access token stops working when it expires on its own, within the access-token lifetime at the latest; the push devices that registered under that session are forgotten in the same transaction, so it stops receiving notifications at once. The session the request itself came from is refused with 403 EC403 and the message "Forbidden: SESSION_END_REFUSED:CURRENT_SESSION" (sign out with `logout` instead). A `sessionId` that is unknown, belongs to another account or tenant, or is already over answers the same 404 EC404, so the route cannot be used to probe for sessions. A `sessionId` that is not a UUID, or any body property, is 422; the per-IP `complete` class answers 429.

get.summary: Read how the signed-in caller signs in: password and linked providers (requires session cookies).

200.description: `passwordStatus.set` is true when the account has a password it can sign in with today; `passwordStatus.canSet` is true when it may set or reset one with the emailed code, which needs a verified login email that is allowed to sign in. `providers` lists ONLY the providers linked to the account, `GOOGLE` before `APPLE`; each carries `canUnlink` and `refusal`, which is `null` when the provider may be unlinked and `NO_OTHER_SIGN_IN` when unlinking would leave the account without a way in. Nothing else about a provider leaves the server: no provider email, no subject, no token. The answer is sent with `Cache-Control: no-store`.

post.summary: Unlink Google or Apple from the signed-in caller account (requires session cookies).

200.description: The provider that was unlinked. The account can no longer sign in with it; signing in with the same provider account again later links it anew, as a first sign-in with that provider does. No session is ended. Unlinking Apple also queues the revocation of the Apple token the server held. It is allowed only while another way in remains: a verified login phone that may sign in, OR a verified login email that may sign in and is not an Apple private relay address (`@privaterelay.appleid.com`, which Apple stops forwarding to once the token is revoked). Otherwise 403 EC403 with the message "Forbidden: SIGN_IN_PROVIDER_UNLINK_REFUSED:NO_OTHER_SIGN_IN" and nothing is written. A provider that is not linked to the account answers 404 EC404; a `provider` outside `GOOGLE` / `APPLE`, or any body property, is 422; the per-IP `complete` class answers 429.

post.summary: Change the password of the signed-in caller with its current password (requires session cookies).

200.description: The credential owner and its new version; no password material ever leaves. The target is always the session actor. Every OTHER session of the account is signed out at once, access tokens included; only the calling session, the one the request refresh-token cookie names, goes on, and the response sets its fresh active-token and refresh-token cookies (never a token in the body). Without a live refresh-token cookie no session is kept and no cookie is set. A wrong current password is 401 EC412 (USER_MISTAKE_PASSWORD_OR_EMAIL), which is NOT the end of the session: the session ends only with 401 EC401; an account without a password is 404 EC404 (set one with `set-password` instead); a current or new password shorter than 8 characters or longer than the allowed length, a missing field or an extra body property is 422.

post.summary: Send a set-password OTP to the signed-in user own login email (requires session cookies).

200.description: Acknowledgement of the delivery channel only. The target is always the caller own login email, taken from the session, so the request carries no identifier and the address is never echoed back. Refused with 401 SIGN_IN_NOT_AVAILABLE when that email is not both verified and loginable.

post.summary: Set a new password with the emailed OTP (requires session cookies).

200.description: The credential owner and its new version. A caller without a credential gets version 1, an existing one is bumped and re-enabled. The OTP is single use. Every OTHER session is signed out at once, its access token included. The calling session, the one the request's refresh-token cookie names, goes on: the response sets its fresh active-token and refresh-token cookies, and no token is ever returned in the body. Without a live refresh-token cookie no session is kept and no cookie is set, so the caller signs in again.

get.summary: Preview what deleting the signed-in account would do (requires session cookies).

200.description: Nothing is changed or sent. `allowed` is false with `refusal` BACKOFFICE_ACCOUNT for an account that holds a backoffice role (another administrator deletes it) or NO_VERIFIED_CHANNEL when neither the email nor the phone is verified and allowed to sign in. `codeChannel` is where the code will go (the verified email first, otherwise the verified phone) and `codeDestinationMasked` shows it masked only. `removed` counts what the deletion removes, by item: legalAcceptances, legalNotices (who was told of a new terms version), trackingConsents, appointmentsCanceled (the appointments, relatives included, that have not started), ratings (deleted whole), ratingInvitationsRevoked, questions, notificationsCanceled, notificationPreferences (the switches of the notification centre), pushDevices (the phones registered for push notifications), notificationInboxItems (the lines of the notification list, shown or still waiting for their hour), patientProfiles (anonymized), relatives, favoriteDoctors, profiles; a doctor account adds doctorAppointmentsCanceled (in every office, the patients are told), receivedRatings, doctorRatingInvitationsRevoked, doctorAnswers, articleAuthorships (an article left with no author is unpublished), calendarConnections, offices, doctorProfiles (the public profile goes at once), pendingTransmissions (still sent to the tax authority for at most one month), erpTraders, erpItems, providerMessageTemplates and operationsAlerts. `warnings` holds codes: APPOINTMENTS_IN_PROGRESS when a started or checked-in visit stays with its doctor; for a doctor also FAILED_TRANSMISSIONS (documents the tax authority never accepted), SMS_UNITS_LOST, LICENSE_LOST (a running licence ends with the account) and RECORD_COPY_ON_REQUEST (a copy of the appointment book is given on request, before or after the deletion). `retained` lists what stays, why, and for at most how many years: in the locked archive the accepted terms versions, an abuse measure when the account is banned, rating moderation decisions without text, and the deletion trace (no name, email, phone or health data); DOCTOR_PATIENT_RECORD when past appointments stay in the doctors' records, never shown to the deleted account or publicly; for a doctor DOCTOR_APPOINTMENT_BOOK, DOCTOR_TAX_RECORDS (the issued documents) and PLATFORM_ACCOUNTING (licences and SMS packages).

post.summary: Send the account deletion code to the signed-in user own verified channel (requires session cookies).

200.description: Acknowledgement of the delivery channel only; the address is never echoed back. The body is empty by contract: the account is the session actor. A backoffice account is refused with 403 and its reason; an account without a verified sign-in channel is 401 SIGN_IN_NOT_AVAILABLE. Inside the resend cooldown, over the per-account send cap, over the per-number cap shared with the other phone flows, or over the per-IP `otp-send` class the answer is 429.

post.summary: Delete the signed-in account with the code (requires session cookies).

200.description: The deleted account id and the server instant of the deletion. The session cookies are cleared, and every other session of the account is refused with 401 from its next request on. Appointments that have not started are canceled (their doctors are told as for any cancellation), reviews and questions are deleted, and one notice that the account was deleted goes to the verified email (else phone). The account keeps no email, phone, password, Google link or terms acceptance; the same email or phone can register again as a new, empty account, unless the deleted account was banned, in which case registration (and attaching that phone to another account) answers 403 USER_LOCKED until the abuse measure expires. A confirm that runs at the same time as the first one answers the same values; every later request of the deleted account, a repeated confirm included, is 401 and clears the cookies. A wrong, expired or consumed code is 401; too many wrong codes for the account or for the number, or over the per-IP `otp-verify` class, is 429.

get.summary: List the messages of new legal versions the signed-in account still has to see (requires session cookies).

200.description: D-132: one item per announced version of a legal document addressed to the account (the core documents to every patient and doctor, the doctor terms to doctors only) that it neither accepted nor closed. `inForce` is false while the version is upcoming, before `effectiveAt` (server clock); `seenAt` is when a device first showed it. Nothing locks the account: the message is information, and the same answer serves the app and the web. A closed message never comes back on any device; a newer version is a new item.

post.summary: Report that the message of a new legal version was shown or closed (requires session cookies).

200.description: D-132: `SEEN` stamps the first time the message was shown, `DISMISSED` closes it on every device (and stamps `seenAt` too when it was never reported). A repeated report keeps the first instants. A version that is not the announced one of a document addressed to the account is 404; the acceptance of the terms is not affected.

get.summary: Get the signed-in patient profile (requires session cookies).

200.description: The patient profile of the signed-in tenant user, or null when registration completed but the patient profile does not exist yet. U-168: the login email, the AMKA and the AFM (and those of the relatives) never travel whole. The answer carries `loginEmailMasked` (`e***a@example.gr`: first and last character before the @, whole domain), `amkaMasked` (`•••••••2345`) and `afmMasked` (`•••••6789`) — ready-to-print texts, null when nothing is stored — and has no `loginEmail`, `amka` or `afm` field. The login phone is masked the same way (`loginPhoneMasked`). A client shows these texts as they are and never keeps or sends back a whole value.

put.summary: Update the signed-in patient identifiers (requires session cookies).

200.description: Patient-owned identifiers only: at least one of `amka`/`afm`, an omitted one left untouched; a value replaces the stored one and `null` erases it. An AMKA is 11 digits whose first six are a date, an AFM 9 digits with a valid check digit (separators are dropped), otherwise 422. U-168: the answer is the self view, so the value just written comes back only as `amkaMasked` / `afmMasked`. The values are stored encrypted (U-169). D-132: the legacy `consents` array is no part of the contract and is refused like every unknown field; the terms a person accepted live in the acceptances (`legalAcceptance` of the registration). Gender, date of birth and names live on the user profile and are not writable here.

patch.summary: Fill in the signed-in patient names and date of birth (requires session cookies).

200.description: D-74: the booking prerequisites of D-05 that live on the user profile. Every field is optional and at least one must be sent; an omitted one is left untouched, and a name is merged with the stored one, so `firstName` alone is refused with 422 when no surname is on file. The body is the patient row in its self view (`amkaMasked` / `afmMasked`, no whole identifier), unchanged: read the effect back from GET /appointment/booking-readiness or GET /patient/me. A `dateOfBirth` after today, or further back than 120 years, is refused with 422 (a baby born today passes). A caller without a patient profile is refused with 403 EC017.

post.summary: Create the signed-in patient profile (requires session cookies).

200.description: Creation-only: sets the user profile (names, gender, date of birth, language) and creates the patient row, independently of how the session was obtained. A `dateOfBirth` after today, or further back than 120 years, is refused with 422 (a baby born today passes). A caller that already has a patient profile is rejected with 409 EC415; use GET /patient/me to detect that state. U-168: `patient` is the self view, so an AMKA / AFM sent in the body comes back only as `amkaMasked` / `afmMasked`.

get.summary: List the relatives of a patient (requires session cookies).

200.description: Every relative of the patient, or [] when there is none. U-168 / D-W45-14: the patient who owns them reads `RelativeSelfView` — `amkaMasked` / `afmMasked` (`•••••••2345`, `•••••6789`, null when none is stored) and no `amka` / `afm` field. Only a backoffice role acting on another account reads the whole `RelativeView`.

post.summary: Add a relative to a patient (requires session cookies).

201.description: The created relative, as `RelativeSelfView` for the patient who owns it (U-168: `amkaMasked` / `afmMasked`, never the whole value that was just sent). A patient keeps at most 20 relatives: the 21st answers 422 with `PATIENT_RELATIVES_LIMIT_REACHED` in the message, and the count is taken under a lock of the account, so two adds at the same instant never pass 20. Rate limited per account under the `relatives-write` class, one budget with changing and deleting a relative (429 past it).

patch.summary: Update one relative of a patient (requires session cookies).

200.description: The updated relative, as `RelativeSelfView` for the patient who owns it (U-168). `amka` / `afm` in the body: a value replaces the stored one, `null` erases it, an omitted key leaves it untouched; the form never holds the old value, so it sends only what was typed (D-W45-14). The relative must belong to the patient in the path. Rate limited per account under the `relatives-write` class, one budget with adding and deleting a relative (429 past it).

delete.summary: Delete one relative of a patient (requires session cookies).

200.description: The deleted relative, as it was before deletion (`RelativeSelfView` for the patient who owns it, U-168). Rate limited per account under the `relatives-write` class, one budget with adding and changing a relative (429 past it).

get.summary: List the favorite doctors of the signed-in patient (requires session cookies).

200.description: One flat list, the most recently saved first, at most 100, each item with `savedAt` and the very card of the doctor search, prices included. There is no grouping and no search here: the device filters the list itself. A doctor no longer listed in the marketplace is not in `items` nor in `total`, and comes back if listed again. 403 `EC017` for an account with no patient profile.

get.summary: List the ids of the favorite doctors of the signed-in patient, to draw the hearts (requires session cookies).

200.description: The doctor ids alone, the most recently saved first, at most 100, a doctor no longer listed included. The search and the profile do not say whether a doctor is a favorite: a client reads this once and matches on `doctorId`.

put.summary: Save a doctor to the favorites of the signed-in patient (requires session cookies).

200.description: The saved doctor and when; saving again answers the first `savedAt`. The route takes no body and no query (422). 404 `DOCTOR_NOT_FOUND`, one answer for a doctor that does not exist and one no longer listed in the marketplace. 409 `FAVORITES_LIMIT_REACHED` at 100 favorites. Rate limited per IP under the `favorites` class.

delete.summary: Remove a doctor from the favorites of the signed-in patient (requires session cookies).

204.description: Removed, or never saved: the same answer, no body. The route takes no body and no query (422). Rate limited per IP under the `favorites` class.

put.summary: Cast, change or take back the vote of this device on an article or a FAQ question.

200.description: The vote as stored. The device key travels in the `X-Helpful-Voter` header, a UUID v4 (422 otherwise). With no header the first vote mints one and answers it as `voterKey`, once: the device keeps it and sends it from then on. `none` takes the vote back and mints nothing. A `reason` goes only with `down`. `target` is `article:<slug>` or `faq:<anchor>`: 404 for an article that is not published and for a question that is not in the published FAQ or has no answer. Rate limited per IP under the `helpful-vote` class. There is never a count in this answer.

get.summary: Read the votes of this device: on one target, or on every FAQ question with `kind=faq`.

200.description: Only the votes of the key in `X-Helpful-Voter` (a UUID v4, 422 otherwise). With no header, an unknown key or a target that no longer exists: `[]`. Exactly one of `target` and `kind`. There is never a count in this answer.

get.summary: Read the vote totals per article and FAQ question (requires a backoffice session).

200.description: One row per target, most `down` first unless `sort` says otherwise, default 50 and at most 100 a page; `from` and `to` bound the last change of a vote. `exists` is false, with `title` null, for an article no longer published and a question no longer in the FAQ. `meta.nextCursor` goes in `cursor` for the next page, null on the last one. Never a device hash. 401 without a session, 403 for any role outside the backoffice.

get.summary: List the conversations of the signed-in account, newest first.

200.description: `side` (`all` by default) keeps the conversations where the reader is that side; `archived=1` reads «Προηγούμενες συνομιλίες». Up to 30 a page, `nextCursor` goes in `cursor`. `lastMessage.preview` is one line, cut on the server at 140 characters. `sideCounts` is on the first page: an account holding both sides shows its chips from it. There is never a read state of the other person. Rate limited per IP under `messaging-read`.

post.summary: Open the one conversation with a doctor, or continue it, with a message.

201.description: The same `clientMessageId` answers the same message, so a retry never doubles. 404 for a doctor the public search does not show; 409 `MESSAGING_CLOSED` when the doctor accepts no new conversations; 409 `MESSAGING_BLOCKED`; 409 `MESSAGING_PRE_REPLY_LIMIT` after 3 messages before the first answer; 400 `MESSAGING_SELF`, `MESSAGE_EMPTY` or `MESSAGE_TOO_LONG`; 422 for a body that fails the schema; 429 `MESSAGING_NEW_LIMIT`, `MESSAGING_SEND_LIMIT` or `MESSAGE_DUPLICATE`, with `Retry-After`. The text is plain and comes back as written: render it only as text, never as HTML, and make no link of it.

get.summary: Read a page of a conversation backwards, or poll its new messages.

200.description: Oldest first inside a page. `before` reads backwards, `after` polls forwards, never both; up to 50 a page. On a poll `counterpart` is null and only the new messages and `state` travel. 404 for a conversation that is not the reader's, unknown or of another tenant alike.

post.summary: Send one message in a conversation of the signed-in account.

201.description: The same `clientMessageId` answers the same message, so «Δοκιμάστε ξανά» never doubles. 404 for a conversation that is not the reader's; 409 `MESSAGING_BLOCKED` or `MESSAGING_PRE_REPLY_LIMIT`; 400 `MESSAGE_EMPTY` or `MESSAGE_TOO_LONG`; 422 for a body that fails the schema; 429 `MESSAGING_SEND_LIMIT` or `MESSAGE_DUPLICATE`, with `Retry-After`.

post.summary: Mark a conversation read up to a message, for this side only.

200.description: Only forwards: an older message changes nothing. `unreadCount` is what stays unread after that message. The other person never learns it. 404 for a message outside the conversation.

get.summary: Count the conversations holding something unread, for the badge.

200.description: Conversations, not messages, with none of the archived ones.

get.summary: What the button of a doctor profile opens: the existing conversation, or whether a new one may start.

200.description: Called only when the button is pressed, so the profile carries no statement more. 404 for a doctor the public search does not show, unless a conversation with them exists.

post.summary: Move a conversation to «Προηγούμενες συνομιλίες», for this side only.

200.description: A new message takes it out by itself.

delete.summary: Take a conversation out of «Προηγούμενες συνομιλίες».

200.description: Successful response.

post.summary: Block a conversation: neither side writes until the one who blocked lifts it.

200.description: Successful response.

delete.summary: Lift a block this side placed.

200.description: Successful response.

get.summary: Download a copy of a conversation as plain text.

200.description: `text/plain; charset=utf-8` as an attachment, the file itself and not the JSON envelope. Only someone who takes part; 429 `MESSAGING_EXPORT_LIMIT` past 10 a day, with `Retry-After`.

post.summary: Report a received message to the team, with a reason of the closed set.

201.description: The team sees only this message, not the conversation, and the sender is not told. 400 `MESSAGE_NOT_RECEIVED` for an own message; 409 `MESSAGE_ALREADY_REPORTED`; 429 `MESSAGING_REPORT_LIMIT` past 20 a day, with `Retry-After`.

get.summary: Read «Δέχομαι νέα μηνύματα» of the signed-in doctor.

200.description: Open until the doctor closes it. 403 for an account without a doctor profile.

put.summary: Change «Δέχομαι νέα μηνύματα» of the signed-in doctor.

200.description: Closed, nobody starts a new conversation; the existing ones go on. 403 for an account without a doctor profile.

get.summary: Read what the signed-in patient still has to fill in before booking (MEMBER or DOCTOR session).

200.description: The blockers standing between the signed-in patient and a booking (verified mobile, full name), plus whether booking is possible at all. It belongs to the patient side: a member account, and an account that is also a doctor only when it holds a patient profile (a doctor books another doctor as a patient); otherwise 403. With `doctorId` it also reports `PATIENT_PENDING_LIMIT_REACHED` when that doctor already holds an open request of the PERSON being booked (D-70, counted per person): the account itself, or the relative named by `relativeId` — each relative has a place of its own. A `relativeId` that is not a relative of this account answers like a person with no open request. With `doctorId` naming the doctor profile of this very account it also reports `PATIENT_IS_THE_DOCTOR`, with or without `relativeId`: one account is never both sides of an appointment, and the booking would be refused with 403. With the chosen slot (`officeId` and `startTime`, both together with `doctorId`) it also reports `BOOKING_NOTICE_TOO_SHORT` and `BOOKING_HORIZON_EXCEEDED` under the effective policy of that doctor and office, decided on the SERVER clock — exactly what the booking would be refused with — and `OFFICE_PHONE_REQUIRED` when that office has no phone. `insideCancellationCutoff` says, only with the chosen slot, that the cancellation deadline of that hour has already passed on the server clock, so a patient told nothing else cannot tell that once booked it cannot be cancelled online; `false` without a slot. `firstVisitKnown` (with `doctorId`) is true when that same PERSON — the account itself, or the relative named by `relativeId` — already holds an appointment this doctor accepted (`booked`, `checked_in` or `completed`); the app asks «first visit?» only when it is false. It is null without `doctorId`, and an unknown doctor, a doctor of another tenant or a relative that is not this account's answer false. `patientSmsExpected` (only with the chosen slot, whatever the blockers) says the answer of the doctor will reach the patient by SMS as well as by email: the doctor switched on the patient SMS of every answer of the confirmation mode of that office (MANUAL: confirmed, and rejected or expired; AUTO: confirmed) and has SMS units left now. It is null without a slot, and for an unknown doctor or a doctor of another tenant, which is never asked about.

post.summary: Book an appointment (requires session cookies).

201.description: The created appointment. A patient booking at an office with no phone is refused with 403 `OFFICE_PHONE_REQUIRED`. The booking is decided by the side the account takes in it: naming its own doctor profile as `doctorId` makes it a doctor booking, naming its own patient profile as `patientId` (another doctor) a patient booking, and a booking of a doctor for the patient profile of its own account — by that doctor or by the backoffice, for itself or for a relative of its own (`RELATIVE`) — is refused with 403 `PATIENT_IS_THE_DOCTOR`, the blocker code `getBookingReadiness` reports it with beforehand (one account is never both sides of an appointment; another doctor books the same person by the patient rules; judged on the accounts behind the two profiles). Every id is read in its canonical lower-case text before the side is chosen, so the letter case of an id changes nothing. A patient booking never sends `status`: the doctor confirmation mode decides it (AUTO ⇒ `booked`, MANUAL ⇒ `pending`) and the mode is snapshotted on the row. A MEMBER keeps one `pending` request per PERSON with one doctor (D-70): the account itself and each of its relatives count separately, and a second one for the same person answers 422 `PATIENT_PENDING_LIMIT_REACHED`. `firstVisit` (optional boolean) is the patient's answer to «first visit with this doctor?» and is read back on the appointment: when that person already holds an appointment this doctor accepted (`firstVisitKnown: true` of the readiness) the server stores false whatever is sent; with no answer it stores null, and a booking by the doctor side always stores null. Anything but a boolean, `null` included, answers 422. `services` holds 1 to 10 lines and `patientNote` at most 500 characters (the configured limit may be lower); past either the booking answers 422 and nothing is written. Rate limited per IP under the `booking` class.

get.summary: List the appointments the caller may see (requires session cookies).

200.description: One page ordered by `startTime, id` in the direction of `sortDir`: `asc` (the default, oldest first) or `desc` (newest first). `limit` defaults to the configured page size and is refused past the configured maximum; `cursor` is the opaque `nextCursor` of the previous page and belongs to the `sortDir` it was issued for — a cursor of the other direction is refused (422); `total` is the whole matched set and does not change between pages. `historyBefore` (optional, an ISO date-time; a client reads its tabs with `scope` instead, whose bounds the server sets) keeps ONLY the history: every appointment in a final status (`completed`, `canceled`, `rejected`, `expired`, `no_show`, `unavailable`) whatever its time, and every open one (`pending`, `booked`, `checked_in`) whose `startTime` is before `historyBefore`; an open appointment at or after it is never returned. It combines with every other filter and the role scope, and with `sortDir` and `cursor` in both directions; without it the list is unchanged. `scope` (optional) reads the tab the server bounds by its OWN clock (D-118): for the doctor side (DOCTOR and backoffice) the day is the platform calendar day (Europe/Athens, daylight saving included) — `today` is every open appointment starting today, `upcoming` every open one after today, `history` every final one and every open one before today; for a member `upcoming` is every open appointment from now on and `history` every final one and every open one that started before now, and `today` answers 422. The scopes of one reader are disjoint and together hold every appointment. `scope` sets the time bounds itself, so it is refused (422) beside `from`, `to` or `historyBefore`; it combines with `status`, `sortDir` and `cursor`. `as` (optional, `patient` or `doctor`) names the side an account that is both a doctor and a patient reads: without it a doctor account reads the doctor side, every other app account the patient side and the backoffice its tenant; `as=patient` lists the appointments its own patient profile booked, with the member scopes; `as=doctor` from an account that is no doctor answers 403 and `as` from the backoffice 422. Every item carries `officeTimeZone`, the IANA zone of its office. For a member every item carries `ratingInvitation` and `ratingId` too: a completed visit offers `ratingInvitation` — the `invitationId` its rating form opens (`ratings/{invitationId}`, `getRatingInvitation`) and `expiresAt`, the end of its window — exactly while the invitation itself takes a rating on the server clock (open and not past `expiresAt`, before any worker closes it, D-118) and the visit is not rated yet; whether its doctor may still be rated is answered by `getRatingInvitation`, not here. `ratingId` is the rating the member wrote of the visit, read with `getRating`; the two are never set together. Every other visit, the doctor side and the backoffice read both as `null`. A whole page costs one read of the ratings, and a page with no completed visit none.

get.summary: Read one appointment (requires session cookies).

200.description: The appointment with its service lines and audit log, `officeTimeZone`: the IANA zone its office keeps its hours in, so every hour is shown on the office clock, and `actions`: what the reader may do with it NOW, decided on the server clock by the very rules the writes check (D-118), and `officePhone`: the current number of the office, else the one frozen at booking, null when neither exists — a member cancels a booked visit until its cancellation deadline and a request until its hour (`!canCancel && isPastCancellationCutoff` means the deadline has passed and only the phone is left) and moves strictly before the cutoff and within the move limit, the doctor side answers a pending request, moves a pending or booked one, cancels anything not over, declares the `outcomes` due after the hour and makes the open `correction`. For a member, `cancellationDeadline` is the instant until which the visit is cancelled online, the very one its messages print as «you can cancel until …», and `null` whenever `canCancel` is false: `startTime` minus `cancellationCutoffHours`, exactly on which a cancel is still on time; `startTime` itself for a visit the doctor side put inside its deadline and for a request already inside it, both cancelled until the hour; for a request still outside its deadline it is the deadline that holds once the request is confirmed, while the request itself is withdrawn until its hour. `rescheduleDenial` names why a member may not move the visit, in the order the move asks: `STATUS` (not pending or booked), `AFTER_CUTOFF` (the cutoff has passed, and from the hour on), `LIMIT_REACHED` (the member moved it as often as allowed), `null` exactly when `canReschedule` is true; `reschedulesLeft` is how many moves the member has left (0 with `LIMIT_REACHED`), `null` once the visit is no longer pending or booked ahead. A move by the doctor side or a note never spends one. The doctor side reads all three as `null`, and its `canReschedule` false carries no reason. Booking readiness and an already rated visit are asked by the write itself. `ratingInvitation` and `ratingId` follow the rules of `listAppointments`: the open rating invitation and the rating of a completed visit, for a member only, on every single-appointment answer. The side comes from the appointment itself: its doctor reads it as the doctor side, the holder of its patient profile as a member (a doctor who booked another doctor reads that visit as a patient), the backoffice every appointment of its tenant; everyone else gets the one 403. A member reads every audit line without the explanation of an automatic change, and every line that set the outcome of the visit (a declared outcome, or a status move to `completed`/`no_show` by anyone) without who set it, its reason or its snapshots (`actorRole` null).

patch.summary: Move or amend an appointment (requires session cookies).

200.description: The updated appointment, with its `actions`. A member may move it only before the effective cancellation cutoff and only into a slot that still passes notice, horizon and availability. A member moving a BOOKED visit to an hour whose cancellation deadline has already passed gets 422 `RESCHEDULE_INSIDE_CANCELLATION_CUTOFF` and nothing is written, unless the body carries `acknowledgeInsideCancellationCutoff: true`; a request (`pending`) and the doctor side are never asked. A doctor moves only a pending or booked appointment (403 otherwise), without the patient accepting, and the status does not change. A member who hands a `pending` request to another person (`relativeId`) takes that person's own D-70 place (422 `PATIENT_PENDING_LIMIT_REACHED` when it is taken). Who the visit is for (`bookedForType`, `relativeId`) and the `patientNote` change only while it is pending or booked, for every role (403 otherwise), and a new person carries its own frozen `relativeSnapshot` (null for the account holder). Only a relative the body names in `relativeId` is checked: a relative that does not exist, or one of another account, is refused with 403 `relative does not belong to patient.` (a relative that was deleted too), while a body that names none — a new hour, a note, a move by the doctor side — goes through for a visit whose relative was deleted, which keeps its frozen `relativeSnapshot`. Only the patient of the appointment writes `patientNote` (D-39): a body from the doctor side that carries it is refused with 403. A new person is asked «first visit?» again (D-W3-22): a visit of that person this doctor already accepted stores `firstVisit` false, otherwise the `firstVisit` of the body, or null without it; `firstVisit` comes only from the patient (403 from the doctor side) and only together with a change of the person (422 otherwise). A write that finds the appointment closed in the meantime answers that same 403; one that finds it changed but still open answers 409. `patientNote` holds at most 500 characters (422 past it; the configured limit may be lower). Rate limited per IP under the `booking` class.

post.summary: Cancel an appointment with a reason (requires session cookies).

200.description: The canceled appointment, with its `actions`. `reasonCode` is mandatory and must belong to the list of the caller own role. A member cancels a booked visit until its cancellation deadline: past it the answer is 403 `CANCEL_AFTER_CANCELLATION_CUTOFF` and nothing is written, and the patient calls the office (`officePhone`), whose doctor side still cancels at any hour. A member withdraws a request (`pending`) until its hour, flagged `canceledLate` past the deadline, and cancels until its hour a visit the doctor side put inside its deadline, not flagged. From the hour on the answer is 403. Repeating the call is idempotent. Rate limited per IP under the `booking` class.

post.summary: Accept a pending request (requires a DOCTOR or backoffice session).

200.description: The appointment moved from `pending` to `booked`. Idempotent when it is already booked; a terminal appointment answers 409.

post.summary: Declare what happened at the visit (requires a DOCTOR or backoffice session).

200.description: The appointment after the one-tap answer of the doctor: `ARRIVED` checks it in, `COMPLETED` and `NO_SHOW` settle it from either `booked` or `checked_in`. Answered only once the appointment has started, and only once: an already settled appointment answers 409. Repeating `ARRIVED` on a checked-in appointment is idempotent. An outcome the SYSTEM recorded (`outcomeSource = SYSTEM`) may be corrected into its opposite until `endTime` plus the configured correction window; correcting a completion into a no-show revokes the rating invitation and answers 409 when the patient already rated the visit.

post.summary: Refuse a pending request with a reason (requires a DOCTOR or backoffice session).

200.description: The appointment moved from `pending` to `rejected`. `reasonCode` is mandatory and comes from the reject list; an already booked appointment answers 409.

get.summary: Read one rating invitation of the signed-in patient (requires session cookies).

200.description: The invitation the rating email links to (the app link `ratings/{invitationId}`), as its patient reads it: `status` on the SERVER clock — an `OPEN` invitation whose `expiresAt` has passed reads `EXPIRED` before any worker closes it — `canSubmit`, whether a rating would be accepted now by the very rules the submit checks (open, inside its window, the doctor holding an active marketplace licence, the doctor not being this very account), with `submitBlocker` — the `RatingInvitationSubmitBlocker` code the submit would refuse with, `null` when `canSubmit` — and `ratingId` once rated. `patientName` and `patientInitial` are the author name a rating would be stored and published with now — the trimmed first name and the capital initial of the last name of the account, its Greek name first, else its first one — read by the very code the submit stores them with, `null` when the account holds no name. The doctor and the date of the visit are read from `getAppointment` with `appointmentId`. It belongs to the patient side: a member, and a doctor account that was the patient of another doctor; an invitation of another account, of another tenant or one that does not exist answers the one 403 `rating invitation is not accessible to this account.`

post.summary: Rate the visit of one invitation of the signed-in patient (requires session cookies).

201.description: The created rating as its patient reads it; `overallRating` is computed by the server from the five 1–10 aspects (a whole point is half a star) and published with them on the 0–5 stars, and the rating waits for moderation before the public reads it. One rating per invitation, on the SERVER clock. A refusal names its `RatingInvitationSubmitBlocker` code in the message: 403 `RATING_INVITATION_NOT_OPEN` (already rated, revoked or closed), 403 `RATING_INVITATION_EXPIRED` (past `expiresAt`; the invitation is closed unless something else closed it first), 403 `RATING_PATIENT_IS_THE_DOCTOR` (the doctor of the visit is this very account: one account is never both sides of a visit), 403 `RATING_DOCTOR_LICENSE_INACTIVE` (the doctor holds no active marketplace licence now; the invitation stays open). An invitation of another account or one that does not exist answers the one 403 `rating invitation is not accessible to this account.`; a second rating of one visit answers 409.

get.summary: List the ratings the caller may read (requires session cookies).

200.description: One page ordered newest first (`createdAt desc, id desc`). `limit` defaults to the page size and is refused (422) past the maximum; `cursor` is the opaque `nextCursor` of the previous page, refused (422) when it is not one; `total` is the whole matched set and does not change between pages. `as` (optional, `patient` or `doctor`) names the side an account that is both a doctor and a patient reads: without it a doctor account reads the ratings it received, every other app account the ratings it wrote and the backoffice every rating of its tenant; `as=patient` lists the ratings its own patient profile wrote; `as=doctor` from an account that is no doctor answers 403 and `as` from the backoffice 422. The patient side reads a doctor reply only once it is approved — a pending or rejected reply reads as `NONE`, with no trace in `updatedAt` — and `replyModerationStatus` filters on that visible status. Moderation notes reach the backoffice only, and a moderator id only the moderator.

get.summary: Read one rating (requires session cookies).

200.description: One rating, read on the side the rating gives the account: its doctor reads it as the doctor (its reply with the moderation status), the holder of its patient profile as the patient (a reply only once approved — until then `updatedAt` is the last change of the rating or its moderation, never of the reply), the backoffice every rating of its tenant. No rating response names the tenant. A rating that does not exist, one of another tenant and an account on neither side answer the one 403 `rating is not accessible to this account.`

post.summary: Answer one rating as its doctor (requires a DOCTOR session).

200.description: The rating with the one reply of its doctor, waiting for moderation (`replyModerationStatus` `PENDING`); the patient and the public read it only once approved. An account acting as a doctor — `DOCTOR` as its primary or a secondary role — answers its own ratings only: a rating that does not exist, one of another doctor and one of another tenant answer the one 403 `rating is not accessible to this account.`; a second reply answers 409, also when two replies race.

get.summary: Read the signed-in doctor own notification settings (requires a DOCTOR session).

200.description: Which appointment events the doctor pays an SMS for (D-09), the reminder offsets currently enabled, and `reminderOffsetOptionsHours`: the only offsets an update may contain. A doctor who never saved them reads the defaults with every SMS off.

put.summary: Update the signed-in doctor own notification settings (requires a DOCTOR session).

200.description: The stored settings. The body is a patch: an absent field keeps its current value. A reminder offset outside `reminderOffsetOptionsHours` is refused with 422 (D-15); the target is always the doctor of the session.

get.summary: Read the signed-in doctor SMS balance (requires a DOCTOR session).

200.description: The remaining SMS units across the active packages, the packages themselves, and how many messages were charged this calendar month. Who granted a package is server-side only.

get.summary: List the signed-in doctor SMS usage (requires a DOCTOR session).

200.description: One page ordered by `sentAt desc, id desc`, with the recipient masked. `limit` defaults to the configured page size and is refused past the configured maximum; `cursor` is the opaque `nextCursor` of the previous page; `total` is the whole matched set. `error` names why a line was not sent: besides the delivery reasons, `RECIPIENT_OPTED_OUT` (the patient turned SMS reminders off) and `REMINDER_EXPIRED` (the reminder would have left once the visit began), both with no unit charged.

get.summary: Read the notification centre of the signed-in account (requires session cookies).

200.description: The centre of the signed-in app account, a doctor included: one `PATIENT` section, and a `DOCTOR` section only for an account that acts as a doctor and holds a doctor profile (a doctor reads its patient side here too). Each category lists its channels: `mode` `ALWAYS` (always sent, `enabled` true), `TOGGLE` (a switch, `enabled` its value) or `SET_BY_DOCTOR` (the SMS a doctor offers for its own appointments, `enabled` null); a channel a category does not list does not exist for it. `scope` names a switch that covers part of its category: `NEW_REQUESTS_ONLY`, `LATE_CANCELLATIONS_ONLY` (the doctor SMS, the same values as `getMyNotificationSettings`) and `WHEN_DOCTOR_OFFERS` (SMS reminders, sent only where the doctor offers them). An account that never saved anything reads the defaults (every switch on, the doctor SMS off) with `updatedAt` null. A switch turned off stops also what is already waiting to leave. Push switches are stored and read; push messages start in a later release. A backoffice account answers 403.

put.summary: Change switches of the notification centre of the signed-in account (requires session cookies).

200.description: The centre after the change. `cells` is a patch: each entry names a `TOGGLE` cell by `category` and `channel` once, and the cells it does not name keep their value. An `ALWAYS` or `SET_BY_DOCTOR` cell, a channel the category lacks and a cell named twice answer 422; a cell of the `DOCTOR` side from an account with no doctor profile answers 403 `doctor profile not found for current user.`. The two doctor SMS cells are the same switches as `smsDoctorNewRequest` and `smsDoctorLateCancel` of `getMyNotificationSettings`: one source, written in the same transaction.

put.summary: Register or refresh the push device of this phone for the signed-in account (requires session cookies).

200.description: The device, without its token. `pushToken` is the native APNs (iOS) or FCM (Android) token of `getDevicePushTokenAsync`; `appId` the bundle / application id of the build; `apnsEnvironment` is required for `IOS` (`SANDBOX` for a development build, `PRODUCTION` otherwise) and refused for `ANDROID`. Production accepts only `com.edoctor.app` with `PRODUCTION`. Call it after every sign-in, on every return to the foreground and when the token changes: a device not seen for as long as a session lives stops receiving and is forgotten. It needs a live session (the refresh cookie of a session that was not revoked), else 401. A token registered by another account moves to this one; an account keeps its 10 most recently seen devices. A device of a session revoked from elsewhere (sign-out of every device, password change, ban) stops receiving and must be registered again after the next sign-in. Push messages start in a later release.

post.summary: Forget the push device of this phone for the signed-in account (requires session cookies).

get.summary: List the notifications of the signed-in account, newest first (requires session cookies).

200.description: One page of the caller own notification list, ordered by `occurredAt desc`, with `unreadCount` (every line the account has not opened, whatever the filter). The list holds what changes in the appointments of the account (registered, confirmed, declined, expired, moved, cancelled, not attended), the reminder of a visit, the reviews (the invitation to write one, published or not, a reply) and the questions (answered, not published); never the messages of doctors. A line is written when the thing happens, whatever the switches of the notification centre say, so an account that turned every email and push off still reads it here. `filter` is `new` (not opened yet), `previous` (opened) or `all` (default); `limit` is 1 to 50 (default 20); `cursor` is the opaque `nextCursor` of the previous page, `null` on the last one. A line shows from the moment its message would leave (a reminder appears at its hour, not at the booking) and for 90 days. `kind` is a closed vocabulary of what happened; `icon` is `CALENDAR`, `CLOCK`, `STAR` or `QUESTION`; `title` and `body` are plain text rendered now in `lang` (`el` or `en`, default the language of the account), to be shown as text, never as markup; `body` may be empty; `read` says whether the account opened it. `target` names what the tap opens, never a URL: `APPOINTMENT`, `RATING_INVITATION` or `QUESTION` with its id (a published review and a reply open the appointment); the thing may be gone by then, and the client then stays on the list. No account, email, phone or template is part of a line. The answer is sent with `Cache-Control: no-store`. A `filter`, `lang`, `limit` or `cursor` outside these, or any other query parameter, is 422.

200.description: `marked` is how many lines became read: only the caller own lines that had shown by the moment of the request (a reminder that appears a minute later stays new). `unreadCount` is the count after it. Calling it again marks nothing and answers `marked` 0. Any body property is 422.

post.summary: Mark one notification of the signed-in account as read (requires session cookies).

200.description: The line, now read, and the `unreadCount` after it. Call it when the person taps a line, before opening its `target`. It is idempotent: a line read already answers the same 200. post.summary: Save one or more screen groups of the registration office (requires a session).

200.description: The saved registration after the write, the same `DoctorOnboardingProgressView` the progress read answers (the clients open `missing[0]`). Rate limited per IP under the `onboarding` class, one budget for every registration write (429 past it). A refusal answers 422 with its marker in the message. Each group (`address`, `details`, `amenities`, `paymentOptions`) replaces only its own fields; the server splits `streetLine` into street and number. A first save without `address` answers 409 with `DOCTOR_ONBOARDING_OFFICE_ADDRESS_REQUIRED`, a point outside Greece 422 with `OFFICE_POINT_OUTSIDE_GREECE`, and a detail without its parent (a parking kind without parking, an accessible toilet or parking space without step-free access, an elevator on the ground floor) 422 with `OFFICE_AMENITY_PARENT_MISSING`; to move a stored elevator office to the ground floor, send `details` with `floor: 0` and `amenities` with `elevator: false` in the same POST. `paymentOptions`, when sent, holds 1 to 5 options. A Google address sends `externalPlace.pointProof` exactly as the address search details answered it: only with a valid proof of this account and place is the point kept as Google's, with the time of those details, and the server alone judges a pin moved more than 1 m (D-W3-33); without one the point is the doctor's. The same Google place and point saved again without a new proof keep their stored time. `pinMoved` is accepted and never read.

200.description: The saved registration after the write, the same `DoctorOnboardingProgressView` the progress read answers (the clients open `missing[0]`). Rate limited per IP under the `onboarding` class, one budget for every registration write (429 past it). A refusal answers 422 with its marker in the message. A registration that still lacks a section is refused before any write with `DOCTOR_ONBOARDING_INCOMPLETE` (and `DOCTOR_UNDER_MINIMUM_AGE` or `DOCTOR_TERMS_NOT_ACCEPTED` where they apply); read the progress again and open `missing[0]`. The older checks run first and answer 422 with their own marker: `DOCTOR_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_MISSING` or `DOCTOR_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_UNVERIFIED`, `DEFAULT_DOCTOR_SERVICE_MISSING`, `DEFAULT_DOCTOR_SERVICE_PRICE_INVALID` or `DEFAULT_DOCTOR_SERVICE_DURATION_INVALID`, and `DOCTOR_ONBOARDING_OFFICE_MISSING`, `DOCTOR_ONBOARDING_OFFICE_PHONE_MISSING` or `DOCTOR_ONBOARDING_OFFICE_ADDRESS_MISSING`; a registration without the liability answer is refused with 400, and one without its activation intent with 422 (`activation intent info is required before completion`).

post.summary: Suggest Greek addresses for the typed text (requires a DOCTOR session).

200.description: At most five suggestions and the `sessionToken` of the search: a first call without one receives a new UUIDv4, every next call of the same search sends it back, and a new search after a pick starts without it. `input` is 2 to 120 characters once trimmed (the body itself takes at most 200); a control, zero-width or bidi character, a line or paragraph break or a tab answers 422, and so does a token that is not a UUIDv4. A session that is not a doctor (primary or secondary role) answers 403, an invalid body 422 (an unknown field too). Rate limited per IP under `address-search-address`, per account under `address-search` (an hour) and under `address-search-suggestions-daily` or `address-search-details-daily` (a day: 100 suggestions, 20 details), and for the whole API under `address-search-suggestions-project` or `address-search-details-project` (the quota day of Google: 250 and 200), each answering 429 past it (D-W3-35). The office address of the registration sends it back in `externalPlace.pointProof`, and only then is the point kept as Google's (D-W3-33). Sending the `sessionToken` of the search closes its session. A place outside Greece answers 422 with `ADDRESS_OUTSIDE_GREECE` in the message. A session that is not a doctor (primary or secondary role) answers 403, an invalid body 422 (an unknown field too). 200.description: The canceled document. Canceling a rejected SALE gives NO money back: the payment it recorded stays taken (the cash in the till, the card charge on the card) and a rejected or canceled document can never be credited, so a refund to the patient happens outside this system. Canceling a rejected CREDIT NOTE (its `correlations` carry `REFUND_OF`) does NOT undo the refund it already made: the cash paid out of the till or the reversal on the card stays given back, and its original becomes creditable again (`refundedByDocumentIds` no longer names it), so a new credit note for the same original must not give the money back a second time; a rejected credit note is better corrected or sent again. Its number goes back to the series only when it was the highest one held. A second change of the same rejected document that lost the race is refused with 409.

200.description: The document back in the transmission queue and `COMPLETED`. The worker sends it within a minute; a new rejection makes it `FAILED_TERMINAL` again. post.summary: Hand a document to a delivery channel (requires a DOCTOR session).

201.description: The job and the result of its first run (201). A refused channel is reported on the job, not as an HTTP error. The body names the document (`documentId`, one of this doctor in this office), the station, the `method` (PRINT reprints on this station; SMS and EMAIL send the receipt again, optionally to a new `phone`/`email`) and nothing else (D-118). An SMS sent again is charged, so it must carry the `Idempotency-Key` header (422 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED` without one); an email may carry one. Either is answered only when the server allows it now (`GET …/delivery/documents/{documentId}/follow-up`): not before the provider accepted the document (422 `RECEIPT_NOT_TRANSMITTED`), never for a cancelled or rejected one (422 `RECEIPT_NOT_DELIVERABLE`), an SMS only while the doctor has SMS units (409 `NO_SMS_UNITS`), and only to a recipient named now or kept from the issuance (422 `DELIVERY_RECIPIENT_MISSING`); a replay with the same key returns the first answer and sends nothing, except after a 409 `NO_SMS_UNITS`, which keeps no key: once the doctor has units the same key sends. A phone is one mobile, `69XXXXXXXX` or E.164 (422 `doc0037` otherwise). The rest of the receipt: the issue time, number, totals, link and recipient are built by the server from the document itself, the same way an issuance hands its receipt over, and a body carrying a snapshot, an issue time, a text or a link is refused (422). `documentSnapshot.receiptLink` is the provider link of the document (`signing.qrCode`, the URL its QR prints) or null while there is none; an SMS or email sent now or later carries the link the document has at that moment (worded as in the source system: issuer, series-number and «Περισσότερα:» in the SMS; its whole email — issuer, branch, counterparty, document, totals, payment, notes, transmission details and «Δείτε το παραστατικό εδώ:» — in the email), and without one it carries no link part at all. An unknown document or one of another doctor or office answers 404; a document that is not issued (cancelled, card payment still open, rejected by the provider) answers 422, exactly as the issuance hands it no receipt.

get.summary: List delivery jobs (requires a DOCTOR session).

200.description: The jobs of the filter, with their attempts. A print waiting for the station (a STATION job in PENDING) carries the document as it stands now — the MARK, QR and link the provider returned after the job was written — while its stored snapshot is never rewritten; one whose document no longer gets a receipt (rejected, cancelled), or cannot be read, is not listed.

get.summary: Read one delivery job (requires a DOCTOR session).

200.description: The job with its attempt history. A print waiting for the station carries the document as it stands now; one whose document no longer gets a receipt (rejected, cancelled) answers 422.

post.summary: Retry or redirect a delivery job (requires a DOCTOR session).

200.description: The job and the result of the run the action triggered. `action` is SMS or EMAIL: the receipt of the job's document sent again, optionally to a new `phone`/`email`, under the same rules and the same `Idempotency-Key` handling as a new SMS or EMAIL job (SMS needs the key and an SMS unit). The SMS or email is built from the document as it stands now, with the provider link it has now. A document that no longer gets a receipt (rejected by the provider, cancelled) answers 422 before anything is written or sent. `followUpActions` tells what the till may offer next.

get.summary: Read what may be sent again for one issued document (requires a DOCTOR or backoffice session).

200.description: For SMS and EMAIL, whether the receipt may be sent again now and, when not, the reason (`RECEIPT_NOT_TRANSMITTED` before the provider accepted it, `RECEIPT_NOT_DELIVERABLE` for a cancelled or rejected one, `NO_SMS_UNITS` for an SMS without a unit). The server decides; the till only shows it. `recipient` is the phone and email the receipt last went to, for prefilling. An unknown document or one of another doctor or office answers 404.

DoctorPublicMarketplaceCardView.description: One search item (`/public/doctors`, `/nearby`): `rating.average` on the 0–5 stars the clients draw, and U-45.2 `isPatientsChoice` always present on the wire, judged on those stars by the application.

With an `availability` other than `all` it counts the doctors with a slot among the first candidates up to a fixed cap: `totalIsLowerBound` is true only when that scan stopped at the cap with candidates left, and `total` is then a lower bound, shown «N+» (S-34.6).

DoctorPublicMarketplaceOfficeBookingPoli.description: U-75: the limits a patient reads for one office, its overrides over the doctor's values; `null` if they could not be read.

DoctorPublicMarketplaceProfileRatingView.description: The rating of a profile, all on the 0–5 stars (U-49): `average` over `count` approved ratings and `aspectAverages`.

DoctorPublicMarketplaceReviewPreviewView.description: A public review, the same in the profile `reviewsPreview` and in `/reviews`: `overallRating` and every `aspect` score on the 0–5 stars the clients draw (U-49; an aspect in half stars). `doctorReplyAt` follows `doctorReply`: only an APPROVED reply, otherwise null. The doctor module owns this type and reads the rating tables directly, an accepted in-module read-only precedent.

DoctorPublicMarketplaceCredentialView.description: U-73: one line of the public biography, in the language of the profile, the newest first.

DoctorPublicMarketplaceResponseMetricsVi.description: How fast and how often the doctor answers the requests that wait for a confirmation, over the last `windowMonths` whole months: a word, never minutes. `responseTime` and `responseRatePercent` are null below five judged requests; every value is null before the first computation. The same for a guest and a signed-in viewer.

DoctorPublicMarketplaceOfficeAmenitiesVi.description: Σ-22: the office details only the office page shows; `parking` and `disabilityAccess` stay on the office itself.

ArticlePublicCardView.description: U-92.1: an article of a public list, a card: the body, the sections and the SEO fields travel only by slug.

ArticlePublicListMetaView.description: U-57.3: what `meta` of the public list says: how many articles match in all, and the service it is filtered by.
